industry.why: Double Underweight, carried, with the counter-case the strongest it has been and named: the US ten-year is 4.83% (down 50 basis points in two months; Goldman Sachs, 20 to 26-Nov), 33 basis points from the sector rows' trigger (back to D under 4.5%), Oppenheimer's 2027 theme is 'beneficiaries of lower bond yields' and Bell (20-Nov) likes UK real estate and homebuilders; the table's Underweights led the week's rebound. Held at F because the yield fell as a safety bid inside a tightening of financial conditions (Mark Wilson: 100 to 150 basis points), European yields rose this week with ECB minutes leaning to hikes, and every property sector reads D or F (27-Nov-26 against 25-Sep-26). This is the first row I would lift if the ten-year goes through 4.5% on an easing read. No Pool name, no live holding.

sector.key: N.2. Real estate - commercial landlords (offices and diversified)
sector.why: Double Underweight, carried, matching its industry: valued off a yield and leveraged twice (asset values and refinancing), with the US ten-year 4.83% falling as a safety bid and 33 basis points from the trigger (back to D under 4.5% on an easing read); Bell (Goldman, 20-Nov) likes UK real estate. Relative strength F (27-Nov-26 against 25-Sep-26, not week on week; F prior). The universe's largest property group, none in the Pool. Counter-case: the row where a rates-relief rally costs most.

geography.why: Overweight, from Neutral, on the first country-specific evidence since the row was set: Germany's composite PMI is 55.0, a 56-month high (Goldman Economics, 24-Nov; S&P Global via Pivotus, 23-Nov), with automation data points turning up (Rockwell, Siemens Digital Industries; Danske, 26-Nov) and Bunds forecast at 3.1% by end-2027 (Marshall, 22-Nov); the signed Lists statement asks for a country view wherever there is evidence, and this week there is. Eleven Pool stocks are German-listed. Counter-case: one PMI print is one month, the US tariff lands on the EU at 15% inclusive, Stehn's winter energy squeeze applies to the euro area, and the German Pool names (Bayer, Symrise, Evonik, Talanx, Sartorius, Deutsche Borse among them) are global businesses on which a country letter is a blunt instrument. Back to C on a German PMI read under 52 or a second month of euro area services PMIs falling.

defs.atr: average true range: each day's high to low, stretched to the previous close on a gap, as a % of the previous close; L5D the last 5 sessions, L1M and L3M the last 30 and 91 calendar days
defs.top_half: a close above the midpoint of the day's high-low range; an up day closes at or above the previous close; days with no range are left out
